summary: Observation of a bright red light phenomenon, initially fixed then moving with a changing shape: lack of information.
description: On June 5, 1955, at 8:55 PM, three witnesses in Cavaillon observed a bright red rectangle in the sky for 20 seconds, directed west of the Luberon mountain range. Initially stationary, the phenomenon then moved very rapidly, changing shape (first as a crescent moon, then as a sphere) towards the east. It shrank and then disappeared. Astronomical analysis ruled out the moon as the cause. The airplane hypothesis was abandoned. GEIPAN classified this case as Category C due to a lack of information and corroboration.

summary: Observations of the SE-NW passage of a luminous phenomenon followed by a multicolored trail: probable observation of the passage of a meteoroid.
description: On May 20, 1955, at 2:30 a.m., two gendarmes observed a luminous phenomenon moving from southeast to northwest. This intrigued them and the phenomenon disappeared within seconds. It was shaped like a shell and was followed by a luminous, multicolored trail. A gendarmerie report was filed. GEIPAN classified this case as category B: probable observation of a bolide, meaning the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Observation of the passage of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a meteoroid.
description: On January 19, 1955, at approximately 10:10 PM, three people observed a luminous phenomenon moving from northeast to southwest. They described a bright white disc followed by a long orange trail. No sound was heard during the five seconds of observation. The police investigation failed to locate any other witnesses to the phenomenon, apart from one person who claimed to have seen something but could not specify the date. GEIPAN classifies this case as category B: probable observation of a bolide, meaning the atmospheric reentry of a meteoroid.

summary: Successive observations of luminous phenomena between 1955 and 1975: lack of information.
description: witness reported three UFO sightings via email in January 2009. Unfortunately, he no longer remembered the exact dates (the first two in 1955/1960 in Remiremont (88) and in the suburbs of Nancy (54), and the third in 1975 in Guadeloupe). The date of January 1, 1955, is arbitrarily given for the first observation of the movement of a luminous phenomenon. The witness reported seeing a circular luminous object, approximately 50 meters in diameter, about 400 or 500 meters from the road and 50 meters above the ground, on a Sunday evening around 5 or 6 PM. Despite our request for further details regarding each sighting, no questionnaires were returned. GEIPAN classifies these sightings as C: lack of information.
